core_obligations: Choose elements of the ideal of definition whose images generate its quotient by the closure of the square, and let the ideal they generate be the candidate finitely generated ideal (proof lines 1722-1724).

Show by induction on powers that the candidate ideal together with the closure of every power of the given ideal equals the given ideal: start from the sum identity and use the description of the square of a sum of ideals, then iterate (proof lines 1724-1729).

Conclude that the closure of the candidate ideal is the given ideal, and hence that the closures of its powers are the closures of the powers of the given ideal, which form a fundamental system of open ideals (proof lines 1729-1732).
Apply the auxiliary statement on finite generation of an ideal of definition to conclude that the ring is adic (proof lines 1733-1734).
proof_roadmap: Choice of the finitely generated candidate ideal (proof lines 1722-1724).
Induction showing the candidate has the given ideal as closure (proof lines 1724-1729).
Identification of the fundamental systems of power closures (proof lines 1729-1732).
Conclusion by the auxiliary finite generation statement (proof lines 1733-1734).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a weakly adic topological ring is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition as soon as some ideal of definition has the property that its quotient by the closure of its square is a finitely generated module (statement lines 1713-1718). The proof uses the characterisation of weakly adic rings and proceeds by an induction on powers: generators of that quotient are chosen and lifted to elements of the ideal, and the identity expressing the ideal as the sum of the ideal they generate and the square closure is iterated, using the description of the square of a sum of ideals, to show that the ideal they generate together with the closure of every higher power is the whole ideal (proof lines 1720-1729). Consequently the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen elements is the ideal of definition itself, so that the closures of the powers of that finitely generated ideal are exactly the closures of the powers of the given one and therefore form a fundamental system of open ideals; the auxiliary statement on finite generation then gives the conclusion (proof lines 1729-1734). The claim is H2: the induction is carried out explicitly and its consequence -- that the closures of the powers of the finitely generated ideal agree with those of the given ideal -- is what makes the definition of adicness apply.
